key_insight: TRCGL-Net boosts rare-disease chest X-ray classification by combining synthetic tail-class data generation with attention and label-co-occurrence modeling.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve detection of underrepresented chest X-ray findings in imbalanced multi-label datasets, supporting more reliable AI-assisted image interpretation.
method: Text-guided conditional diffusion generates realistic tail-class X-ray samples from disease semantics.
Channel reweighting and class-aware attention emphasize lesion-relevant features and regions.
A label co-occurrence graph convolution network propagates information across disease categories.
evidence_signal: On the PadChest dataset, the method reached tail-class mAP 0.4904, overall mAP 0.4408, and mAUC 0.8989, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in the abstract.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and realism of generated images and on label-co-occurrence patterns that may not transfer cleanly across institutions or datasets.
paper_title: TRCGL-Net: A Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification Framework with Generative Data Augmentation and Label Co-Occurrence Modeling
